note: What a server sends to tell a client something happened. The sort is named first and settles what follows; unlike WorldEvent it carries no source apart from what the sort itself carries. The header names the unit the event is about.

fields.name: event
fields.note: Which event, from 0 to 140, and so which fields follow.

fields.name: subject
fields.note: The unit the event is about.

fields.name: stage
fields.note: A client reads it and shows nothing for it; a server writes zero.

fields.name: damage
fields.note: How much harm, and from what.

fields.name: physical
fields.note: Physical damage.

fields.name: magical
fields.note: Magical damage.

fields.name: true
fields.note: True damage.

fields.name: sourceKind
fields.note: What sort of source it was.

1.name: item
1.note: An item the killer holds, named by script.

fields.name: script
fields.note: The spell or effect, by the number its name gives, shown by name.

fields.name: parentScript
fields.note: The spell or effect it came from, by the number its name gives, shown by name.

fields.name: parentCaster
fields.note: What it carries is not recorded for this range; a server writes zero.

fields.name: parent
fields.note: Where the spell or effect came from.

bits.name: source
bits.note: What sort of source the parent spell or effect is, numbered as sourceKind is.

bits.name: side
bits.note: What it means is not recorded for this range; a server writes zero.

bits.name: category
bits.note: A client sums two entries of this sort where this, the source kinds and both spells match, and, where this is zero, the subjects match too.

bits.name: spellLevel
bits.note: The rank of the spell, as shown.

bits.name: unused
bits.note: Unused; a server writes zero.

fields.name: spent
fields.note: How much gold, as shown.
